entries.title: Ben Shelton v Carlos Alcaraz
entries.hook: Shelton brings home support and a sharpened game to the defending champion's quarterfinal test.
entries.synopsis: Ben Shelton went straight from beating Stefanos Tsitsipas to the practice court: reaching this quarterfinal was a step, not the destination. Carlos Alcaraz brings the defending champion's authority into an Ashe night session where Shelton can make the occasion feel very different. The American's challenge is to sustain that pressure against a player no American has beaten at a major.

facts.statement: Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz faces eighth seed Ben Shelton in the US Open quarterfinals.
Shelton defeated Stefanos Tsitsipas in the fourth round before returning to the practice court.
Shelton is seeking to become the first American to defeat Alcaraz at a Grand Slam.
Shelton and Alcaraz are second on the Arthur Ashe night-session programme.

entries.title: Aryna Sabalenka v Linda Noskova
entries.hook: Sabalenka's title defence and No. 1 hopes meet Wimbledon champion Noskova in the last eight.
entries.synopsis: Aryna Sabalenka needs the title to keep a chance of retaining No. 1, making this quarterfinal a test of both her New York defence and her standing in the game. Linda Noskova arrives with the authority of a Wimbledon champion. With Rybakina, Pegula and Gauff also in the ranking contest, this is a direct collision between two major winners with consequences beyond the next round.

facts.statement: Sabalenka must win the US Open to retain a chance of keeping the No. 1 ranking.
Linda Noskova enters this quarterfinal as the reigning Wimbledon champion.
Rybakina, Pegula and Gauff also remain in contention for the No. 1 ranking.
Sabalenka and Noskova open the Arthur Ashe programme at 11:30am New York time.

entries.title: Jessica Pegula v Emma Navarro
entries.hook: Pegula and Navarro put a guaranteed American semifinal place on the line, with a ranking prize still within Pegula's reach.
entries.synopsis: Jessica Pegula has a previous US Open final appearance; Emma Navarro is trying to turn her return to the last eight into another deep run at home. Their meeting guarantees an American semifinalist, but only one can keep building on a tournament that has brought six home players into the singles quarterfinals. Pegula also remains among the players who can leave New York as world No. 1.

facts.statement: Pegula and Navarro meet in an all-American US Open quarterfinal.
Pegula reached the 2024 US Open final, losing to Sabalenka.
Their quarterfinal guarantees an American woman in the singles semifinals.
Pegula remains one of four women with a chance of taking the No. 1 ranking.
Pegula and Navarro open the Arthur Ashe night session on Tuesday.

entries.title: Frances Tiafoe v Alex Michelsen
entries.hook: Tiafoe and Michelsen meet with an American semifinal place guaranteed and the home-title drought still alive as a target.
entries.synopsis: Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen can draw on the same home crowd, but this quarterfinal gives only one of them a place in the last four. They are part of a six-player American singles contingent in the quarterfinals, the country's largest here since 2002. Their match converts that collective promise into a guaranteed semifinal berth; the successful player carries it into the closing days.

facts.statement: Tiafoe and Michelsen face each other in the US Open quarterfinals.
Six Americans reached the singles quarterfinals, the most at the US Open since 2002.
The Tiafoe-Michelsen match guarantees an American man a semifinal place.
Tiafoe and Michelsen play in the Arthur Ashe day session after Sabalenka and Noskova.

entries.title: Italian Grand Prix race
entries.hook: Monza earns a five-star replay: two starts and split Mercedes strategies turn a home race into a contest worth watching in full.
entries.synopsis: The Italian Grand Prix keeps changing its terms: an early red flag resets the field, Mercedes lets its drivers contest the lead, and a virtual safety car forces a choice between track position and fresher tyres. There is a separate fight between the McLarens, with little room to spare. It earns our five-star replay recommendation for the way those decisions unfold, rather than simply for the final classification.

facts.statement: Antonelli won at Monza after starting nineteenth on the grid.
Antonelli became the first Italian winner at Monza since 1966.
Mercedes split strategies under a virtual safety car, with Antonelli stopping and Russell staying out.
Antonelli finished ahead of Russell and Verstappen in the official race classification.

entries.hookSpoilerOn: Antonelli wins from nineteenth at Monza, ending a sixty-year wait for an Italian home winner.
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Kimi Antonelli turned nineteenth on the grid into victory, using fresh tyres after a virtual-safety-car stop to catch George Russell. Mercedes finished first and second, with Max Verstappen third. The comeback made Antonelli the first Italian to win at Monza since 1966; the split strategy and the battles behind make the full race worth revisiting.

entries.title: Panthers v Roosters
entries.hook: The minor premiers meet fourth-placed Sydney with a week off within reach.
entries.synopsis: Penrith secured top spot in the final round. Nathan Cleary faces Daly Cherry-Evans in a qualifying final that rewards the winner with direct passage to a preliminary final. The loser gets another chance, but must play next week.

facts.statement: Penrith finished first and the Roosters fourth.
Penrith secured the minor premiership in the final round.
Cleary and Cherry-Evans are the named halfbacks.
Qualifying winners advance to preliminary finals; losers enter semi-finals.

entries.title: Warriors v Dolphins
entries.hook: The Dolphins begin their first finals campaign against second-placed New Zealand.
entries.synopsis: The Dolphins arrive with Cobbo, Finefeuiaki and Nikorima returning. The Warriors regain Ford and Halasima for a qualifying final offering the winner a week off. A defeat preserves one life but adds a sudden-death semi-final to the route.

facts.statement: This is the Dolphins’ first finals appearance.
The Warriors finished second and the Dolphins third.
Ford and Halasima return for New Zealand.
The winner advances directly to a preliminary final.

entries.title: Sharks v Cowboys
entries.hook: Trindall returns for Cronulla as fifth meets eighth with no second chance.
entries.synopsis: Trindall rejoins Hynes after a shoulder injury. The Cowboys regain Neame, Nanai and Laybutt, but their eighth-place finish leaves them on the elimination path. The winner must then get past a qualifying-final loser to reach the preliminary finals.

facts.statement: Cronulla finished fifth and North Queensland eighth.
Trindall returns after a shoulder injury.
Neame, Nanai and Laybutt return for North Queensland.
The loser is eliminated; the winner enters a semi-final.

entries.title: Rabbitohs v Knights
entries.hook: Sixth meets seventh to open the finals, with one season ending on Friday.
entries.synopsis: South Sydney and Newcastle begin on the sudden-death side of the draw. Ponga is named at fullback for the Knights, opposite Dufty. Winning this elimination final earns another game against a top-four opponent; losing ends the premiership campaign.

facts.statement: South Sydney finished sixth and Newcastle seventh.
This elimination final opens the series on Friday.
Ponga and Dufty are the named fullbacks.
The winner faces a qualifying-final loser in a semi-final.

entries.title: Daniel Merida v Andrey Rublev
entries.hook: Merida tests his rapid rise against Rublev’s established New York record.
entries.synopsis: Daniel Merida arrived in New York ranked 39th after beginning the year outside the top 160. Andrey Rublev brought four US Open quarterfinal appearances to this second-round meeting: a useful measure of whether the Spaniard’s first ATP title in July signalled a lasting step forward.
entries.hookSpoilerOn: Daniel Merida 6(3)-7(7) 6-2 6-4 6-4 Andrey Rublev
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Merida recovered from losing the opening tiebreak to win in four sets, the biggest victory of his career. Daniel Merida 6(3)-7(7) 6-2 6-4 6-4 Andrey Rublev.

facts.statement: Merida rose from No. 163 in January to No. 39 before the US Open.
Rublev entered as the 23rd seed and a four-time US Open quarterfinalist.
Daniel Merida v Andrey Rublev was scheduled in Round 2 at Court 11.

entries.title: James Duckworth v Yibing Wu
entries.hook: Duckworth and Wu meet at the point where return pressure can change the match.
entries.synopsis: James Duckworth’s second-round assignment was Yibing Wu, with a place in the last 32 at stake. Court 6 offered a close view of the serve-and-return contest between the Australian and Chinese players; the official match record makes those exchanges the useful starting point for the replay.
entries.hookSpoilerOn: James Duckworth 5-7 3-6 1-6 Yibing Wu
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Wu won 7-5, 6-3, 6-1, converting five of 14 break opportunities while facing none himself. His 36 winners against 12 unforced errors explain the increasing separation. James Duckworth 5-7 3-6 1-6 Yibing Wu.

facts.statement: Wu converted five of fourteen break points and faced no break points.
Wu recorded 36 winners and 12 unforced errors.
James Duckworth v Yibing Wu was scheduled in Round 2 at Court 6.

entries.title: Dino Prizmic v Tommy Paul
entries.hook: Paul’s home campaign meets Prizmic’s challenge in the Grandstand.
entries.synopsis: Tommy Paul brought the twentieth seed and local support into this second-round match against Dino Prizmic. Their Grandstand meeting put a place in the last 32 on the line, with the American trying to build a route towards the second week of his home major.
entries.hookSpoilerOn: Dino Prizmic 2-6 3-6 7-5 4-6 Tommy Paul
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Paul won 6-2, 6-3, 5-7, 6-4 in three hours and four minutes. Prizmic’s third-set response forced the American to finish the work in a fourth. Dino Prizmic 2-6 3-6 7-5 4-6 Tommy Paul.

facts.statement: Paul entered as the twentieth seed in the men’s singles draw.
Paul and Prizmic played for three hours and four minutes in the Grandstand.
Dino Prizmic v Tommy Paul was scheduled in Round 2 at Grandstand.

entries.title: Alexei Popyrin v Alejandro Tabilo
entries.hook: Popyrin faces seeded Tabilo with another Australian place in the last 32 at stake.
entries.synopsis: Alexei Popyrin’s path through Grigor Dimitrov led to a second-round meeting against Alejandro Tabilo. The Chilean held the twenty-fifth seed, making this a test of whether Popyrin could carry that first-round progress further through the draw.
entries.hookSpoilerOn: Alexei Popyrin 6-2 6(4)-7(7) 6(3)-7(7) 2-6 Alejandro Tabilo
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Tabilo won 2-6, 7-6(4), 7-6(3), 6-2. Two middle-set tiebreaks reversed Popyrin’s opening advantage in a three-hour, 22-minute match. Alexei Popyrin 6-2 6(4)-7(7) 6(3)-7(7) 2-6 Alejandro Tabilo.

facts.statement: Tabilo was seeded twenty-fifth in the men’s singles draw.
The match lasted three hours and twenty-two minutes on Court 7.
Alexei Popyrin v Alejandro Tabilo was scheduled in Round 2 at Court 7.

entries.title: Jakub Mensik v Jurij Rodionov
entries.hook: Mensik and Rodionov arrive from straight-set opening wins.
entries.synopsis: Jakub Mensik’s seventeenth seed met Jurij Rodionov’s opening-round momentum in this second-round match. Mensik had come through Shintaro Mochizuki in three sets, while Rodionov had done the same against Giovanni Mpetshi Perricard. The contest put two efficient starts against one another for a place in round three.
entries.hookSpoilerOn: Jakub Mensik 6-3 3-6 6-2 6-3 Jurij Rodionov
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: The official fixture result is available below. Jakub Mensik 6-3 3-6 6-2 6-3 Jurij Rodionov.

facts.statement: Mensik beat Shintaro Mochizuki in three sets in the opening round.
Rodionov beat Giovanni Mpetshi Perricard in three sets in the opening round.
Jakub Mensik v Jurij Rodionov was scheduled in Round 2 at Court 11.

entries.title: James Duckworth / Miomir Kecmanovic v Marcelo Melo / John Peers
entries.hook: Duckworth and Peers stand on opposite sides of an Australian doubles interest.
entries.synopsis: James Duckworth paired with Miomir Kecmanovic against Marcelo Melo and John Peers in the opening round. With an Australian on each side, this Court 15 meeting offered two different partnerships chasing the same place in round two.
entries.hookSpoilerOn: James Duckworth / Miomir Kecmanovic 6-3 5-7 4-6 Marcelo Melo / John Peers
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Melo and Peers recovered from a set down to win 3-6, 7-5, 6-4 in one hour and 41 minutes. James Duckworth / Miomir Kecmanovic 6-3 5-7 4-6 Marcelo Melo / John Peers.

facts.statement: Melo and Peers won the second set 7-5 after losing the opening set.
The Court 15 match lasted one hour and forty-one minutes.
James Duckworth / Miomir Kecmanovic v Marcelo Melo / John Peers was scheduled in Round 1 at Court 15.

entries.title: Alexander Bublik v Tommy Paul
entries.hook: Paul and Bublik revisit the third-round rivalry that went the distance a year ago.
entries.synopsis: Alexander Bublik ended Tommy Paul’s 2025 US Open in five sets at this same stage. Their rematch carried that history into Louis Armstrong Stadium, where Paul was again playing for the chance to take his home campaign into the second week.
entries.hookSpoilerOn: Alexander Bublik 4-6 6-3 7(7)-6(4) 1-6 3-6 Tommy Paul
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Paul reversed last year’s outcome in another five-set match, recovering from two sets to one down. A 6-1 fourth set and a 5-0 start to the fifth turned the contest before he closed it 6-3. Alexander Bublik 4-6 6-3 7(7)-6(4) 1-6 3-6 Tommy Paul.

facts.statement: Bublik beat Paul in five sets in the third round of the 2025 US Open.
Paul won the fourth set 6-1 and led 5-0 in the fifth before closing it 6-3.
Alexander Bublik v Tommy Paul was scheduled in Round 3 at Louis Armstrong Stadium.

entries.title: Jakub Mensik v Learner Tien
entries.hook: Mensik and Tien bring a young rivalry into the pressure of a home major.
entries.synopsis: Learner Tien faced Jakub Mensik in the third round with his best US Open run taking shape. Mensik arrived as the new mixed doubles champion alongside Karolina Muchova, giving the Czech a very different kind of New York momentum.
entries.hookSpoilerOn: Jakub Mensik 3-6 6-1 7(7)-6(2) 3-6 4-6 Learner Tien
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Tien won 6-3, 1-6, 6-7(2), 6-3, 6-4, recovering from two sets to one down to continue his best run at his home Grand Slam. Jakub Mensik 3-6 6-1 7(7)-6(2) 3-6 4-6 Learner Tien.

facts.statement: Mensik won the 2026 US Open mixed doubles title with Karolina Muchova.
Tien recovered from two sets to one down against Mensik.
Jakub Mensik v Learner Tien was scheduled in Round 3 at Louis Armstrong Stadium.

entries.title: Tommy Paul v Carlos Alcaraz
entries.hook: Paul tests the returning defending champion for a place in the quarterfinals.
entries.synopsis: Carlos Alcaraz arrived with the stronger head-to-head record and a lighter workload through three rounds. Paul had taken the longer route, including a five-set encounter with Bublik. Their fourth-round meeting asked whether that match toughness could disrupt the defending champion’s increasingly assured return from a wrist injury.
entries.hookSpoilerOn: Tommy Paul 4-6 3-6 4-6 Carlos Alcaraz
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Alcaraz won 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 to reach his fifth US Open quarterfinal in six appearances. Tommy Paul 4-6 3-6 4-6 Carlos Alcaraz.

facts.statement: Alcaraz entered the match with a 6-2 head-to-head advantage over Paul.
Paul reached round four after a five-set victory over Alexander Bublik.
Tommy Paul v Carlos Alcaraz was scheduled in Round 4 at Arthur Ashe Stadium.

entries.title: DJ Bennett / Ava Esposito v Storm Hunter / Desirae Krawczyk
entries.hook: Hunter and Krawczyk begin their seeded doubles campaign against an American pair.
entries.synopsis: Storm Hunter and Desirae Krawczyk entered as the thirteenth seeds against DJ Bennett and Ava Esposito. The Australian-American pairing had an immediate opportunity to establish itself in a draw led by Siniakova and Townsend; Bennett and Esposito stood between them and round two.
entries.hookSpoilerOn: DJ Bennett / Ava Esposito 0-6 3-6 Storm Hunter / Desirae Krawczyk
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Hunter and Krawczyk won 6-0, 6-3 to advance. DJ Bennett / Ava Esposito 0-6 3-6 Storm Hunter / Desirae Krawczyk.

facts.statement: Hunter and Krawczyk were seeded thirteenth in women’s doubles.
Hunter and Krawczyk won their opening match 6-0, 6-3.
DJ Bennett / Ava Esposito v Storm Hunter / Desirae Krawczyk was scheduled in Round 1 at Court 13.

entries.title: Magali Kempen / Alexandra Panova v Storm Hunter / Desirae Krawczyk
entries.hook: Hunter and Krawczyk face a pair fresh from the Cincinnati final.
entries.synopsis: Magali Kempen and Alexandra Panova brought a Cincinnati doubles final into their second-round match with Storm Hunter and Desirae Krawczyk. The thirteenth seeds were trying to keep their own campaign moving towards a possible meeting with the top seeds.
entries.hookSpoilerOn: Magali Kempen / Alexandra Panova 4-6 7-5 4-6 Storm Hunter / Desirae Krawczyk
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Hunter and Krawczyk won 6-4, 5-7, 6-4, earning a third-round meeting with Siniakova and Townsend. Magali Kempen / Alexandra Panova 4-6 7-5 4-6 Storm Hunter / Desirae Krawczyk.

facts.statement: Kempen and Panova reached the Cincinnati Open women’s doubles final.
Hunter and Krawczyk won this match in three sets to reach round three.
Magali Kempen / Alexandra Panova v Storm Hunter / Desirae Krawczyk was scheduled in Round 2 at Court 12.

entries.title: Katerina Siniakova / Taylor Townsend v Storm Hunter / Desirae Krawczyk
entries.hook: Hunter and Krawczyk stand in the path of Siniakova and Townsend’s missing major.
entries.synopsis: Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend entered this third-round meeting with three different Grand Slam titles together and the US Open still to add. Storm Hunter and Desirae Krawczyk, seeded thirteenth, were the immediate obstacle to the top seeds’ quarterfinal place.
entries.hookSpoilerOn: Katerina Siniakova / Taylor Townsend 7(8)-6(6) 6-4 Storm Hunter / Desirae Krawczyk
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Siniakova and Townsend recovered from 5-3 down in the opening set and won 7-6(4), 6-4. Their 35 winners against 15 from Hunter and Krawczyk supplied the decisive attacking difference. Katerina Siniakova / Taylor Townsend 7(8)-6(6) 6-4 Storm Hunter / Desirae Krawczyk.

facts.statement: Siniakova and Townsend entered with titles together at the other three Grand Slams.
Siniakova and Townsend hit 35 winners against Hunter and Krawczyk’s fifteen.
Katerina Siniakova / Taylor Townsend v Storm Hunter / Desirae Krawczyk was scheduled in Round 3 at Louis Armstrong Stadium.

entries.title: Sydney Swans v Fremantle
entries.hook: Sydney face Fremantle at the SCG with a Grand Final place on the line.
entries.synopsis: Sydney bring the SCG and a week to prepare; Fremantle bring minor-premier form and the momentum of a semi-final win. This is a direct test of Sydney's pressure against Fremantle's ability to turn the home-and-away season into a finals win. The winner advances to the Grand Final, while the loser is finished.

facts.statement: Sydney host Fremantle at the SCG with a Grand Final place on the line.
Sydney have a week to prepare, while Fremantle arrive from a semi-final win.
The winner advances to the Grand Final and the loser is eliminated.
Sydney hosts Fremantle at the SCG on Friday 18 September at 7.40pm AEST.

entries.title: Hawthorn v Brisbane Lions
entries.hook: Hawthorn host Brisbane at the MCG with a Grand Final place on the line.
entries.synopsis: Hawthorn have the week off behind them and the MCG in front of them; Brisbane arrive with back-to-back premiership experience and a strong recent record at the ground. The matchup is Hawthorn's preparation and pressure against Brisbane's finals know-how. The winner advances to the Grand Final, while the loser is finished.

facts.statement: Hawthorn host Brisbane at the MCG with a Grand Final place on the line.
Hawthorn have a week to prepare before hosting Brisbane at the MCG.
Brisbane bring back-to-back premiership experience, while Hawthorn must convert preparation into pressure.
Hawthorn hosts Brisbane at the MCG on Saturday 19 September at 5.15pm AEST.

entries.title: NRL Finals Week 2
entries.hook: Two semi-finals, two remaining preliminary-final places, and no second chances.
entries.synopsis: Roosters-Sharks at Allianz on Saturday and Warriors-Knights at Eden Park on Sunday complete the next step of the bracket. The Roosters have a chance to reverse last season's finals loss to Cronulla. Auckland then gets a home knockout with Kalyn Ponga directing Newcastle's challenge. Both winners advance; both losers are finished.

facts.statement: Two semi-finals, two remaining preliminary-final places, and no second chances.
Roosters-Sharks at Allianz on Saturday and Warriors-Knights at Eden Park on Sunday complete the next step of the bracket.

The Roosters have a chance to reverse last season's finals loss to Cronulla. Auckland then gets a home knockout with Kalyn Ponga directing Newcastle's challenge. Both winners advance; both losers are finished.
NRL Week 2 comprises Roosters v Sharks at Allianz Stadium on Saturday and Warriors v Knights at Eden Park on Sunday.

entries.title: Sydney Roosters v Cronulla-Sutherland Sharks
entries.hook: Cronulla bring continuity; the Roosters face another sudden-death meeting with Walker still sidelined.
entries.synopsis: Sam Walker remains unavailable with an ankle injury. Angus Crichton is expected back from his foot problem, while Egan Butcher is out with concussion and Salesi Foketi is named to start in the back row. Cronulla expect no late changes. That contrast puts the focus on combinations under pressure, with a preliminary-final place on the line.

facts.statement: Cronulla bring continuity; the Roosters face another sudden-death meeting with Walker still sidelined.
Sam Walker remains unavailable with an ankle injury.

NRL Week 2 comprises Roosters v Sharks at Allianz Stadium on Saturday and Warriors v Knights at Eden Park on Sunday.

entries.title: New Zealand Warriors v Newcastle Knights
entries.hook: Eden Park’s knockout afternoon tested Newcastle against the Warriors in front of a record New Zealand rugby league crowd.
entries.synopsis: The match is complete. The result and key passages are available when you reveal results; the outcome remains protected here.

facts.statement: Eden Park gives the Warriors the home stage; Ponga gives Newcastle a route to disrupt it.
The named halves are Te Maire Martin and Chanel Harris-Tavita for the Warriors, against Sandon Smith and Fletcher Sharpe for Newcastle.
Kalyn Ponga starts at fullback for the Knights. The question is which spine can control a knockout afternoon when one mistake can end the season. Kick-off is Sunday at 4.05pm AEST.
NRL Week 2 comprises Roosters v Sharks at Allianz Stadium on Saturday and Warriors v Knights at Eden Park on Sunday.

Newcastle Knights defeated New Zealand Warriors 12–10. Dom Young’s early second-half try put Newcastle ahead at Eden Park. The Knights then resisted sustained late pressure, earning a preliminary final against Penrith and ending the Warriors’ season.

entries.hookSpoilerOn: Newcastle Knights defeated New Zealand Warriors 12–10.
entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Dom Young’s early second-half try put Newcastle ahead at Eden Park. The Knights then resisted sustained late pressure, earning a preliminary final against Penrith and ending the Warriors’ season.

entries.title: MotoGP Austrian Grand Prix
entries.hook: Marquez and Martin arrive level on points; Austria could separate them before the flyaways.
entries.synopsis: Marc Marquez returns to the Red Bull Ring as last year's winner, tied with Jorge Martin at the top of the championship. Martin says the weekend will test whether his arm-pump problem needs surgery. Pedro Acosta adds a home-manufacturer challenge for KTM. Watch how sustained braking pressure affects that title duel over the race.

facts.statement: Marquez and Martin arrive level on points; Austria could separate them before the flyaways.
Marc Marquez returns to the Red Bull Ring as last year's winner, tied with Jorge Martin at the top of the championship.

Martin says the weekend will test whether his arm-pump problem needs surgery. Pedro Acosta adds a home-manufacturer challenge for KTM. Watch how sustained braking pressure affects that title duel over the race.
Austria is the final stop before the flyaway races begin.

entries.title: Geneva Sail Grand Prix - race day 1
entries.hook: Geneva opens the final three-event run with fresh crew combinations to settle quickly.
entries.synopsis: The eleventh stop of the championship puts the fleet back on Lake Geneva. Kahena Kunze returns to Brazil for the remaining three events, making communication and coordination an immediate storyline. Saturday establishes the event position from which teams must attack Sunday; clean early races matter when the season has so little room left.

entries.title: Geneva Sail Grand Prix - race day 2
entries.hook: Geneva's deciding day puts the new combinations under pressure with two season stops left.
entries.synopsis: Sunday closes the Switzerland event before the championship's final two rounds. Brazil's returning double Olympic champion Kahena Kunze is one crew change to watch as the fleet converts Saturday's work into an event finish. The sporting question is who leaves Geneva with momentum for the final stretch, rather than merely one fast race.

entries.title: Zimbabwe v Australia - 2nd ODI
entries.hook: Australia’s second Harare ODI tested the new batting combinations again, with the series at stake.
entries.synopsis: The match is complete. The result and key passages are available when you reveal results; the outcome remains protected here.

facts.statement: Zimbabwe will co-host the 2027 ODI World Cup.
Raza captains with Ngarava injured; Taylor and Cremer return.
Australia are rebuilding their middle order after senior retirements.
The second and third ODIs are on 18 and 20 September in Harare.

Australia defeated Zimbabwe by 84 runs. Travis Head made 112 from 84 balls as Australia posted 6/356. That batting platform secured an unassailable 2–0 series lead, although Billy Stanlake’s injury interrupted his return.

entries.synopsisSpoilerOn: Travis Head made 112 from 84 balls as Australia posted 6/356. That batting platform secured an unassailable 2–0 series lead, although Billy Stanlake’s injury interrupted his return.

entries.title: Zimbabwe v Australia - 3rd ODI
entries.hook: The final Harare ODI brought Australia’s Zimbabwe leg to a close before the tour moved to South Africa.
entries.synopsis: The match is complete. The result and key passages are available when you reveal results; the outcome remains protected here.

entries.title: Australia v South Africa — First ODI
entries.hook: Durban opens a new test of Australia’s ODI combinations, with Cummins and Starc joining the squad for the South African leg.
entries.synopsis: Australia’s rebuilding batting order now faces South Africa after the Zimbabwe leg. Cummins and Starc are in the squad, though selection and workloads remain match-by-match decisions. The opener starts a three-game contest that doubles as preparation for the 2027 World Cup and October’s Tests.

facts.statement: Durban hosts the first of three ODIs on 24 September.
Cummins and Starc join the ODI squad for South Africa.
The six African ODIs form part of Australia’s preparation for the 2027 World Cup.

entries.title: Australia v South Africa — Second ODI
entries.hook: Pink Day at the Wanderers puts Australia’s first response under scrutiny, with only one ODI left after Johannesburg.
entries.synopsis: After Durban, this is the chance to turn an opening advantage into a series win or recover lost ground. The scoreline must decide which story applies. Pink Day gives the middle match its own occasion, while Australia still have to balance ODI combinations against the coming Test workload.

facts.statement: The Wanderers hosts the annual Pink Day ODI on 27 September.
Johannesburg is the middle match of the three-ODI series.
Australia’s leading fast bowlers are using the white-ball tour to prepare for the Tests.

entries.title: Australia v South Africa — Third ODI
entries.hook: Potchefstroom closes Australia’s six-match ODI tour before attention turns to red-ball preparation.
entries.synopsis: The final ODI is the last chance to settle this series and leave a selection impression in the format. Whether it is a decider depends on Durban and Johannesburg. The tour then changes emphasis: a two-day warm-up precedes the three Tests.

facts.statement: The third ODI is scheduled for 30 September at JB Marks Oval.

entries.formCopy: Sydney arrived through a 36–20 win over the Dolphins. Newcastle earned their place by beating Penrith 22–14 with 12 men, keeping the Panthers scoreless after half-time. The Roosters bring attacking momentum; the Knights bring evidence that they can absorb severe pressure and still find a way through.
entries.closingCopy: Sandon Smith now has the chance to win a premiership against the Roosters, the club he left after they signed Daly Cherry-Evans. Cherry-Evans is preparing for his final NRL match, while Mark Nawaqanitawase is heading back to rugby union. Newcastle’s revival meets a Sydney side with farewells riding on the same result.

entries.title: All Blacks v Wallabies
entries.hook: Australia bring renewed belief to Eden Park; New Zealand bring a changed captain and a record nobody in gold has broken for decades.
entries.formCopy: The All Blacks arrive from a demanding four-Test series against South Africa. Australia come off a confidence-building meeting with the same opposition. That contrast makes this a test of recovery and composure, not just reputation: New Zealand need to settle quickly after a long spell away, while the Wallabies must carry their recent momentum into a much less forgiving setting.
entries.closingCopy: For Australian supporters, Eden Park turns optimism into a familiar question: can this group make belief survive the difficult moments? For New Zealand, protecting home ground is bound up with protecting the Bledisloe itself. Codie Taylor takes the captaincy while Ardie Savea recovers from shoulder surgery; Scott Barrett returns after back surgery. Those changes add a leadership test to the rivalry, without settling the starting team before it is announced.
entries.synopsis: The opening Bledisloe Test is at Eden Park on Saturday 10 October, before the return match in Sydney a week later. New Zealand are chasing a 25th consecutive home-ground Test win over Australia here and have held the trophy since 2003. The Wallabies need a performance that keeps the two-match contest alive rather than allowing the venue's history to dictate the evening. Final selections remain unannounced; squad recalls are not a confirmed match-day lineup.
entries.changeReason: New captain, injury absences and recalled leaders materially change the preview; replace incomplete two-section context.

entries.title: Bathurst 1000
entries.hook: Toyota joins the Mountain fight as reshuffled driver pairings chase the Great Race and the final Enduro Cup places.
entries.formCopy: Most endurance partnerships have changed for 2026: only six combinations carried over unchanged from last year. Chaz Mostert stays with Fabian Coulthard, while Ryan Wood now shares with Jaxon Evans. Matt Payne is paired with Will Davison and Broc Feeney with Nick Percat. Familiar names are therefore not always familiar units; the co-driver stints are part of the competitive picture, not a pause between star turns.
entries.closingCopy: Bathurst asks teams to trust somebody else with the car they have worked on all year. For supporters, a season of manufacturer loyalty becomes a very personal day of hope and nerves; Toyota's first full Supercars season adds a new side to that argument. For crews and co-drivers, execution matters as much as the headline name. Garry Rogers Motorsport's returning wildcard brings another emotional thread, with Nathan Herne and James Moffat carrying the revived team name.
entries.synopsis: The Bathurst 1000 starts at 11:30am Sydney time on Sunday 11 October at Mount Panorama. Its 161 laps cover roughly 1000 kilometres around a 6.213km circuit, ending the Ryco Enduro Cup before the championship Finals Series. That makes the day about more than one trophy: the endurance title guarantees a Finals berth, with the post-enduro top ten also advancing. Toyota's GR Supra now contests the season alongside Ford and Chevrolet; reliability, driver changes and pit work must hold up over the full distance.
entries.changeReason: Current driver partnerships, Toyota entry and Finals qualification consequences justify complete four-section endurance preview.

entries.title: Liverpool v Manchester City
entries.hook: Liverpool's rebuild meets Manchester City's fight to defend both points and the legitimacy of its success.
entries.formCopy: Andoni Iraola is reshaping Liverpool around aggressive pressing and quicker counter-attacks. Enzo Maresca's City retain a possession-led approach, with central overloads intended to release their wide players. At Anfield, the sporting test is whether Liverpool can turn City's attempts at control into opportunities to break, rather than simply chase the ball.
entries.closingCopy: For Liverpool supporters, the case puts fairness alongside the familiar desire to beat a rival. For City fans, pride in their club meets scrutiny of how its success was financed. That is the emotional tension, not a claim that supporters or today's players are responsible for accounting decisions. Management face reputational and regulatory uncertainty; the players still have a match to win. City's appeal and the pending sanction process mean neither a final punishment nor a rewritten honours list should be treated as settled.
entries.synopsis: Liverpool host Manchester City at Anfield on Monday 12 October, 2:30am Sydney time. Beyond the points, the fixture carries the weight of the Premier League Commission's findings on City's financial reporting and spending-rule breaches between 2009/10 and 2017/18. These are not salary-cap rules. City disputes the findings and confirmed it lodged an appeal on 1 October. Sanctions remain to be decided separately. The match does not resolve that case, but it brings questions about sporting credibility into one of the league's sharpest rivalries.
entries.changeReason: Published Commission findings and newly lodged appeal change the rivalry context; complete all four distinct preview sections.

facts.statement: The independent Commission found serious financial reporting and spending-rule breaches across 2009/10 to 2017/18; sanctions await a separate hearing.
Manchester City says it lodged an appeal on 1 October 2026 and disputes the findings.

entries.title: Australia v New Zealand — Rugby League World Cup
entries.hook: Australia's title defence begins against a confident New Zealand, with its first-choice halfback missing and selection still unsettled.
entries.formCopy: New Zealand arrive as the 2025 Pacific Cup champions; Australia bring the momentum of an Ashes series win. The Kiwis' forward depth gives them a platform to challenge the defending world champions, rather than wait for an upset. Australia's task has become harder with Nathan Cleary ruled out, while the fitness of Isaah Yeo and Dylan Edwards remains uncertain.
entries.closingCopy: This rivalry is about who owns the green-and-gold standard, not just who wins opening night. Kevin Walters must rebuild Australia's attacking direction without Cleary; Sam Walker is a contender, not a confirmed selection. For New Zealand, the old Sydney Football Stadium's seven-match losing record offers a history to overturn at the rebuilt Allianz. The 2008 champions showed why an opening defeat need not define a World Cup, but neither side wants to spend this tournament recovering lost ground.
entries.synopsis: The men's Rugby League World Cup opens at Allianz Stadium on Thursday 15 October. Australia and New Zealand share Pool A with Fiji and Cook Islands, with only the top two progressing to the semi-finals. The result will shape that route without deciding the trophy. Australia's squad is expected after the NRL Grand Final; announced selections, rather than predicted teams, will determine the final matchups.

entries.title: Australia v New Zealand
entries.hook: Sydney gives the Wallabies a home-ground chance to challenge New Zealand's long hold, with a World Cup reunion already on the calendar.
entries.formCopy: Australia enter the Bledisloe fortnight buoyed by their recent Springboks performance; New Zealand have come through a demanding four-Test South Africa series. Codie Taylor captains the All Blacks while Ardie Savea recovers from shoulder surgery, with Scott Barrett returning after back surgery. Those are the current squad-level changes, not a confirmed Sydney starting XV.
entries.closingCopy: For Wallabies supporters, home advantage is an invitation to believe rather than accept another familiar ending. For New Zealand, protecting a trophy held since 2003 is a matter of standards as well as silverware. Les Kiss is building towards a home World Cup; Taylor must lead through an injury-hit period. This same stadium hosts the countries' first World Cup pool meeting next October, giving both teams a chance to shape the atmosphere of a rivalry that will return on an even bigger stage.
entries.synopsis: Australia host New Zealand at Accor Stadium on Saturday 17 October, one week after the first Bledisloe Test at Eden Park. This closes the Wallabies' home Test programme before their northern tour. Whether Sydney can decide the cup depends on Auckland's result; that claim should wait until the first match is played. The teams meet here again in the 2027 World Cup pool stage, on 9 October.
